2027-02-12.title: First Friday of the Great Fast
2027-02-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-02-12.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). Abstinence from meat; fasting is highly recommended on all the Fridays of the Great Fast.
2027-02-12.verse: Then the Lord said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” He said, “I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?”
theo: Yesterday God asked Adam, “Where are you?” Today he asks Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” Sin that began as distrust of God quickly turns against the brother. Cain and Abel both bring offerings; God regards Abel's, and Cain's face falls. God speaks to him like a father warning a son: “If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin is lurking at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it.” Cain does not master it. He leads his brother into the field and kills him. When God asks where Abel is, Cain answers with a lie and a shrug: “I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?” But the earth cannot keep the secret: “Listen; your brother's blood is crying out to me from the ground!” And yet even here God shows mercy: he puts a mark on Cain “so that no one who came upon him would kill him.” Jesus speaks to the root of Cain's sin, the comparing and judging eye: “Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.” “Why do you see the speck in your neighbor's eye, but do not notice the log in your own eye?” “You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your neighbor's eye.”

On the Fridays of the Great Fast our parishes walk the Way of the Cross, often in the evening, and many keep a stricter fast. Abel's blood cried from the ground for justice; on the Cross we see another blood, “the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel”, the blood that cries for mercy. The second reading shows the Jordan in flood at harvest time. As soon as the feet of the priests carrying the ark touch the edge of the water, the river stands up “in a single heap”, and the whole people crosses on dry ground. Twelve men lift twelve stones from the riverbed, so that when the children ask, “What do those stones mean to you?”, the answer will be told. Paul holds up Abraham as the father of all who believe: “Hoping against hope, he believed.” He knew his body was “already as good as dead” and Sarah was barren, yet “No distrust made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, being fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised.” These words were written for us too, who believe in the God who raised Jesus, “who was handed over to death for our trespasses and was raised for our justification.” Every Friday of the Great Fast walks toward that Friday, and through it to Easter.
outline: Ask: who is the brother or sister God has placed in your keeping?
Sin lurking at the door; Abel's blood cries out.
Abraham's faith, and stones from the Jordan.
The judging eye healed by the Cross.
live: Walk the Way of the Cross
Join your parish for the Way of the Cross this evening, or pray it at home with your family.
Visit or call one relative or neighbour you have neglected, and ask what they need.
2027-02-12.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, your blood speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. Master the sin that lurks at the door of our hearts, take the log from our eyes, and make us keepers of our brothers and sisters. Give us the faith of Abraham, hoping against hope, and lead us through the waters of these days to your Easter. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we receive the Blood of Christ, which does not cry for vengeance like Abel's but for mercy and peace.

quick: God asks: where is your brother? We are our brothers' keepers.
Abraham hoped against hope and believed God's promise.
First take the log out of your own eye.
2027-02-12.action: Walk the Way of the Cross today, at church or at home.
2027-02-12.question: Whom do I judge, and what is the log in my own eye?

family.explain: Cain was jealous of his brother Abel and hurt him very badly. God asked Cain: where is your brother? Cain said: I do not know; am I my brother's keeper? But God wants us to look after one another. Every brother and sister is a gift from God.
family.intention: We pray for brothers and sisters who are quarrelling.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we look after each other better in our family?”

illus: A man in Alappuzha used to criticise his neighbour's drinking at every parish gathering. One Lenten Friday, at the station where Jesus falls the third time, he suddenly remembered his own temper at home, and how his children went quiet when he came in. That evening he went to his neighbour's house, not to preach, but to ask him to walk the Way of the Cross with him the next Friday. The neighbour came. Both of them, the man said later, had logs to carry.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this Friday of the Great Fast we stand before your Cross. Look on us with mercy. Amen.
share: Where is your brother Abel? (Genesis 4:9). Whom am I neglecting?
Hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). Where do I need Abraham's faith?
First take the log out of your own eye (Matthew 7:5). What do I need to see in myself?
interc: For the Church as she walks the Way of the Cross this Friday.
For victims of violence and for those who have killed.
For brothers and sisters divided by jealousy or property.
For those who have lost hope.
For our group, that we may stop judging one another.
pm.close: Father, the blood of your Son speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. Make us keepers of one another and give us the faith of Abraham. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, God asked Adam: where are you? Today he asks Cain: where is your brother Abel? (Genesis 4:9). Sin against God soon becomes sin against the brother. Cain answers: am I my brother's keeper? God's answer is yes.

God had warned Cain: sin is lurking at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it (Genesis 4:7). Jealousy began with comparing. That is why Jesus says: do not judge. First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly (Matthew 7:5).
Abraham teaches us another way: hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). He did not look at his weakness but at God's promise. And Israel crossed the Jordan because God held back the waters.

Today is a Friday of the Great Fast. As we walk the Way of the Cross, we see the blood of Jesus, which speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. Let us become keepers of our brothers and sisters. Amen.
kids: Children, God asks each of us: where is your brother? where is your sister? Jesus wants us to take care of each other. Do something kind for your brother, sister or friend today.

intro: Cain's question, Abraham's hope, the stones of the Jordan, and the eye that judges.

sub: A better word from the Cross.
q: Then the Lord said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” He said, “I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?”
Those who say, “I love God,” and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars; for those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen.
points.apply: Do one concrete thing this week for a brother, sister or neighbour in need.

sub: A body as good as dead.
q: And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.
Hoping against hope, he believed that he would become “the father of many nations,” according to what was said, “So numerous shall your descendants be.”
points.apply: Bring one hopeless situation to God every day of this week.

q: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me.
You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your neighbor's eye.
points.apply: Each time you are tempted to criticise someone today, name one of your own faults instead.

concl: God asks where our brother is, and the Cross answers with mercy.
Keep your brother, hope against hope, and let Christ heal your eyes.
2027-02-12.resolve: Walk the Way of the Cross on every Friday of the Great Fast.
